marker: # unit_length is the repeat unit each locus actually steps by, checked against eight S. aureus
# genomes: N315, Mu50, MW2, COL, MRSA252, MSSA476, NCTC 8325 and USA300. The flanking length of a
# locus does not change between strains, so every product of that locus must leave the same
# remainder when divided by the repeat unit.
# THE THREE SER-ASP LOCI STEP BY 6 bp, NOT THE 18 bp THE PAPER DESCRIBES. The Introduction calls
# the R region repeat an 18-nucleotide unit, which is three Ser-Asp dipeptides, but a dipeptide is
# two codons and the array gains or loses them one at a time. Across the eight genomes every
# observed step at clfA, clfB and sdr is a multiple of 6 and not of 18, and the remainders collapse
# to a single value only at 6 bp: clfA 7 distinct sizes from 997 to 1303, clfB 6 from 816 to 936,
# sdr 14 from 556 to 796. The 18 bp figure is kept in scheme.yml as what the paper states.
#   spa  consistent at the 24 bp the paper gives
#   ssp  consistent at the 9 bp tripeptide unit the paper gives
# ref_size is the product these primers give in the NCTC 8325 assembly GCA_000013425.1 by in
# silico PCR. NCTC 8325 is the control strain the paper itself types, as isolate 34. The paper
# publishes no product sizes at all, so there is nothing to compare these with; they are recorded
# because the scheme has to be anchored somewhere.
# sdr HAS NO ref_size BECAUSE IT HAS NO SINGLE PRODUCT. One primer pair amplifies sdrC, sdrD and
# sdrE together by design. Six of the eight genomes give the three products the paper expects;
# NCTC 8325 and MRSA252 give two, so the reference is one of the two strains where a gene of the
# array is absent or diverged at a primer site. The locus is declared in known_multiple so that
# the one product per marker checks skip it, and a call for it is flagged MULTIPLE.
# ref_repeats IS EMPTY THROUGHOUT, SO THIS SCHEME SIZES ITS MARKERS WITHOUT CALLING THEM. The
# method is read as a band pattern on a gel, not as a per locus allele: the paper assigns each
# distinct pattern an arbitrary number, 1 to 26 in Table 1, and publishes no amplicon sizes, no
# repeat numbers and no reference values of any kind. A profile from this scheme is therefore not
# comparable with those pattern numbers. The eight genome comparison fixes each flanking length
# only up to a whole number of repeats, so it cannot supply the missing count either, and no copy
# number is recorded because none is published and none can be pinned down.
